en: I bow to Lord Rāma, the joy of the solar dynasty, who has been honored by the gods in their distress, and whose forehead is beautifully adorned with sandalwood paste.
I bow to Lord Rāma, the performer of the sacrifice for the Lord of Sages, the remover of the calamity of the stone, and the shatterer of the great bow. || 2 ||
I bow to Lord Rāma, who carries out the words of his own father, who dwells in the forest of asceticism, and who holds a beautiful bow in his hand.
I bow to Lord Rāma, who released the deer from his arrow, who granted liberation to Jaṭāyu, and who cast down the leader of the monkeys. || 4 ||
I bow to Lord Rāma, who gained the consent of the monkey hosts, who bound the lord of rivers (the ocean), and who brought about the destruction of the lineage of the ten-faced Rāvaṇa.
I bow to Lord Rāma, who causes joy to the gods, showers the desired objects upon the monkeys, and draws away the grief of his own kinsmen.
I bow to Lord Rāma, who has vanquished his enemies, who protects the kingdom, who consumes the suffering of his subjects, and whose very nature is the destruction of the darkness of ignorance.
I bow to Lord Rāma, the sun that dispels the darkness of the world, who removed all mountains as ornaments and brought the city back to its own abode.
A person who, with a concentrated mind, recites this Aṣṭaka of the Best of the Raghus without interruption, does not experience the fear born of worldly existence.
Thus ends the Śrī Rāmāṣṭaka composed by the venerable Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmānanda.
